scenes.name: Born in golden armor
scenes.display: Karṇa, son of Sūrya, was born wearing golden armor and earrings, fused to his flesh. No weapon could slay him.
scenes.tts: Kar-na, son of Soor-ya, was born wearing golden armor and earrings, fused to his flesh. No weapon could slay him.

scenes.name: Surya's warning
scenes.display: One night Sūrya warned him in a dream: Indra would come as a brāhmaṇa to beg the armor away — and to give it was to die.
scenes.tts: One night, Soor-ya warned him in a dream. Indra would come as a brahmin to beg the armor away; and to give it, was to die.

scenes.name: Karna's resolve
scenes.display: But Karṇa would not be shamed by refusing a beggar. His fame as the greatest of givers outweighed a long life.
scenes.tts: But Kar-na would not be shamed by refusing a beggar. His fame as the greatest of givers outweighed a long life.

scenes.name: Indra at noon
scenes.display: As Karṇa worshipped the noon Sun, an old brāhmaṇa came begging for the kavacha and kuṇḍala. It was Indra.
scenes.tts: As Kar-na worshipped the noon Sun, an old brahmin came begging for the ka-va-cha and koon-da-la. It was Indra.

scenes.name: The flaying gift
scenes.display: Karṇa did not flinch. Smiling, he cut the armor and earrings from his own body. The wounds closed — but now he could die.
scenes.tts: Kar-na did not flinch. Smiling, he cut the armor and earrings from his own body. The wounds closed; but now, he could die.

scenes.name: The Vasava Shakti
scenes.display: Moved, Indra gave him the Vāsavī Śakti — a dart that never misses, but only once. Karṇa kept it for Arjuna; fate would spend it elsewhere.
scenes.tts: Moved, Indra gave him the Vaa-sa-vee Shak-ti. A dart that never misses, but only once. Kar-na saved it for Ar-ju-na; but fate would spend it elsewhere.
